attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation still assumes the Yang-Mills-specific boundary OPE decomposition \(N=\Gamma\circ M+A\) with \(A\ge0\) and \(\Gamma\ge0\) for reflected Wilson hairpin products. The formal finite-dimensional argument is valid, but the constructive/RG analysis has not yet proved that the actual Wilson collar singularity has this positive multiplicative-plus-additive form, nor that its connected boundary kernel \(C_\partial\) vanishes.
steps: Start with the regulated reflection-positive quadratic form \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i,F_j)\ge0\) on gauge-invariant collar observables. For fixed \(\delta>0\), apply this to \(T_\delta F_i\) to obtain positive matrices \(N^{(\delta)}\).

Use the cutoff-removal topology only where it is known to be valid: finite reflected collar probes. Hence \(N^{(\delta)}\to N\) entrywise and \(N\ge0\) by closedness of the positive semidefinite cone.

Model the singular approach to the reflection plane by the finite-matrix boundary decomposition \(N=\Gamma\circ M+A\), where \(M\) is the intended target OS matrix, \(\Gamma\) is multiplicative, and \(A\) is additive.

Eliminate positive additive contacts: if diagonal trace continuity gives \(A_{ii}=0\), then \(|A_{ij}|^2\le A_{ii}A_{jj}=0\), so \(A=0\). This shows additive contacts are not the generic obstruction unless their positivity or diagonal control fails.

With \(A=0\), the same-theory target is \(M=\Gamma^{[-1]}\circ N\). To transfer positivity from every possible collar matrix \(N\ge0\), the reciprocal anomaly must act as a positive Schur multiplier, equivalently \(\Gamma^{[-1]}\ge0\).

If the anomaly \(\Gamma\) is also a positive boundary kernel, normalize it by \(\gamma_{ij}=\Gamma_{ij}/(\Gamma_{ii}^{1/2}\Gamma_{jj}^{1/2})\). Positivity of \(\Gamma\) gives \(|\gamma_{ij}|\le1\); positivity of \(\Gamma^{[-1]}\) gives \(|\gamma_{ij}|\ge1\). Therefore \(|\gamma_{ij}|=1\) for all \(i,j\).

Equality in the Gram Cauchy-Schwarz inequality forces all normalized boundary vectors to be collinear, so \(\gamma_{ij}=u_i\overline u_j\) and \(\Gamma_{ij}=d_i\overline d_j\). This is merely a diagonal congruence and does not change OS positivity.

For a rank-one anomaly, the logarithmic cross-ratio cancels: \(K_{ik;jl}=0\). Conversely, a nonzero \(K\) detects a nonrank-one connected boundary OPE term and yields a finite-matrix obstruction to same-theory positivity transfer.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The branch has reduced the problem to a sharp finite-matrix invariant, but it has not supplied the hard estimate: a no-connected-boundary-OPE theorem for coincident reflected Wilson footprints in four-dimensional Yang-Mills. Without that estimate, the closed-cone argument proves only collar OS positivity, not full same-theory OS positivity at the reflection plane.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: boundary OPE cross-ratio localization

assumptions: For each fixed \(�delta>0\), the cutoff OS quadratic forms on \(T_\delta\mathcal W_+\) converge in a topology strong enough to pass every finite reflected matrix entry to the limit.
The collar-limit matrix \(N=[N_{ij}]\) is positive semidefinite for every finite Wilson family, by regulated reflection positivity and closed-cone transfer.
The boundary OPE/trace expansion is valid in the finite-matrix sense: \(N_{ij}=\Gamma_{ij}M_{ij}+A_{ij}\), with \(\Gamma_{ij}\ne0\).
Diagonal trace continuity has already been proved for the chosen Wilson core, so no additive diagonal defect remains: \(A_{ii}=0\).
The additive contact matrix \(A\), if present, is a positive semidefinite boundary covariance matrix.
The multiplicative boundary anomaly \(\Gamma\), after diagonal normalization, is a positive semidefinite boundary kernel generated by the same reflected Wilson collar limit.
The desired bridge is universal on finite OS matrices: positivity of all possible collar-limit matrices \(N\) must imply positivity of the intended matrices \(M\) without changing the theory.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms \(S_{a,L}\) on lattice or cutoff gauge-invariant Wilson observables, together with collar embeddings \(T_\delta\mathcal W_+\subset\{t\ge\delta\}\) and finite reflected quadratic forms \(Q_{a,L}\).

target object: continuum OS-positive Schwinger functions \(S\) on the same gauge-invariant Wilson algebra \(\mathcal W_+\), yielding the OS Hilbert space after quotient by null vectors, a vacuum vector, and a positive Hamiltonian.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, controlled first on fixed collars by closedness of finite OS cones and then at \(t=0\) by boundary trace limits of reflected Wilson matrix entries.

same-theory condition: the observables \(F_i\), their collars \(T_\delta F_i\), and their limits are identified without adding boundary counterterms, changing Wilson-loop renormalization at the reflection plane, or replacing \(M\) by a boundary-renormalized matrix \(N\).
\(N_{ij}\) denotes the positive collar-limit OS matrix obtained from \(\Theta T_\delta F_i\cdot T_\delta F_j\).
\(M_{ij}\) denotes the intended OS matrix of the continuum Yang-Mills Schwinger functions on the locked test algebra.
\(\Gamma_{ij}\) is the multiplicative boundary anomaly produced by coincident reflected Wilson footprints; rank-one means \(\Gamma_{ij}=d_i\overline d_j\) with all \(d_i\ne0\).
\(A_{ij}\) is an additive contact term; when it is a positive boundary covariance and has zero diagonal, Cauchy-Schwarz forces \(A=0\).

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Compute a finite family of reflected Wilson hairpins with coincident boundary footprint and find \(K_{ik;jl}\ne0\), or find a nonzero additive contact with zero diagonal that is not positive semidefinite. Either outcome is a falsifier of this same-theory OS bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma converts the remaining reflection-positivity problem from an abstract topological closure issue into a finite Wilson boundary OPE invariant. The closed-cone part is already valid on collars; the lemma states that the only same-theory-compatible boundary multiplicative anomaly is a diagonal congruence, so all nonrank-one connected boundary cumulants are genuine obstructions.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let \(\mathcal W_+\) be a locked dense gauge-invariant Wilson collar algebra in the positive time half-space. For each finite family \(F_1,\dots,F_n\in\mathcal W_+\), suppose the collar limits of reflected OS matrix entries exist and admit a boundary decomposition \(N_{ij}=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)=\Gamma_{ij}M_{ij}+A_{ij}\), where \(M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j)\) is the intended continuum OS matrix, \(\Gamma\) is a nonvanishing multiplicative boundary anomaly, and \(A\) is an additive boundary contact matrix. If diagonal trace continuity gives \(A_{ii}=0\), \(A\) is positive semidefinite, and \(\Gamma\) is itself a positive boundary kernel, then the same-theory transfer of OS positivity from \(N\ge0\) to \(M\ge0\) for all finite Wilson families is valid exactly when \(\Gamma\) is a rank-one diagonal congruence on the family. Equivalently, every logarithmic cross-ratio \(K_{ik;jl}=\log\Gamma_{ij}+\log\Gamma_{kl}-\log\Gamma_{il}-\log\Gamma_{kj}\) vanishes. A nonzero connected boundary OPE polarization \(K\) is therefore a finite-matrix falsifier of the regulated reflection-positive to continuum OS-positive bridge for the locked theory.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A perturbative or constructive estimate showing a nonzero connected boundary kernel \(C_\partial\) for coincident reflected hairpins produces a concrete falsifier; proving \(C_\partial=0\) on a dense core would promote the bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma proposes a computable infinitesimal falsifier: instead of evaluating arbitrary finite anomaly matrices, compute the connected boundary OPE kernel for small Wilson hairpin deformations. If the kernel is nonzero, some finite cross-ratio is nonzero.
candidate_lemmas.statement:
For a one-parameter family of mirror-smooth Wilson hairpin observables \(F(\mu)\) whose reflection-plane boundary footprint is encoded by a small boundary source \(\mu\), suppose the multiplicative anomaly has the local expansion \(\log\Gamma(\mu,
u)=b(\mu)+\overline{b(\nu)}+C_\partial(\mu,
u)+O(\|\mu\|^3+\|\nu\|^3)\). Then the logarithmic cross-ratio polarizes the connected boundary kernel: \(K(�mu_1,�mu_2;�nu_1,�nu_2)=C_\partial(\mu_1-�mu_2,�nu_1-�nu_2)+O(3)\). Thus vanishing of \(K\) to second order is equivalent to absence of the bilinear connected boundary OPE kernel on that hairpin core.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the boundary OPE decomposition cannot be formulated in the constructive/RG framework, or if a computed Wilson hairpin cross-ratio \(K\ne0\) shows the same-theory OS bridge fails.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves, for a dense mirror-smooth Wilson hairpin core, that the connected coincident-footprint boundary kernel \(C_\partial\) vanishes and that the RG topology controls the corresponding reflected finite OS matrices through the collar trace.
control_decision.reason: The branch continues to produce sharper proof obligations. It has moved from topology, to trace continuity, to finite Schur-multiplier linear algebra, and now to a local connected boundary OPE kernel. This is a substantive narrowing rather than repetition.

dependency_updates.description: The bridge now factors into a formal valid collar closed-cone lemma plus a nonformal boundary OPE theorem. The exact obstruction is the logarithmic cross-ratio of the multiplicative Wilson anomaly after additive contacts are eliminated.

The test algebra must include a dense Wilson collar core with locked normalization and stable reflected products. It is not enough to define individual Wilson loops; mixed OS matrix entries must have same-theory trace limits.
The topology must dominate finite reflected collar matrices and then a boundary trace modulus for products. Entrywise convergence of nonreflected Schwinger functions is insufficient.

dependency_updates.dependency_id: boundary OPE positivity for Wilson collars
dependency_updates.description: Needed to justify \(N=\Gamma\circ M+A\) with \(A\ge0\) and \(\Gamma\ge0\), enabling the finite-dimensional cross-ratio argument.

falsifiers: A direct calculation of reflected Wilson hairpins with coincident boundary footprint giving \(K_{ik;jl}\ne0\) is a same-theory falsifier: the collar-limit matrix may remain positive, but the intended OS matrix is not obtained by a harmless diagonal congruence.
A perturbative cusp or hairpin anomalous factor depending on a mixed pair of loops rather than on the two individual loops separately would falsify the rank-one anomaly criterion.

An additive boundary contact matrix with \(A_{ii}=0\) but \(A_{ij}\ne0\) would falsify the assumed positive-boundary-covariance structure; it would show that Cauchy-Schwarz cannot be used to remove contacts.

If RG compactness controls each Wilson loop separately but not products \(\Theta T_\delta F_i\cdot T_\delta F_j\), the finite OS matrix topology is too weak and the closed-cone passage is not valid for the needed probes.

If the continuum construction silently replaces \(M\) by \(N\) or inserts a boundary counterterm at \(t=0\), positivity may be recovered for a modified theory; that is a falsifier of the same-theory condition, not a proof of Yang-Mills OS positivity.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 190 localizes the remaining obstruction one layer further. The formal closed-cone passage is valid on collars, and positive additive contacts vanish once diagonal trace continuity is known. The only durable same-theory obstruction is therefore a connected multiplicative boundary OPE for reflected Wilson products. Its finite-dimensional invariant is the logarithmic cross-ratio \(K\); infinitesimally, \(K\) is the polarization of a boundary kernel \(C_\partial\) for Wilson hairpins. Thus the next Yang-Mills estimate is not generic reflection positivity preservation, but proving \(C_\partial=0\) on the locked Wilson core or finding a nonzero hairpin kernel as a falsifier.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work out a model calculation for two mirror-smooth Wilson hairpins with the same boundary footprint but different tangential jets. Express the mixed collar anomaly in terms of a boundary OPE coefficient, compute the polarized cross-ratio to second order in the jet difference, and check whether known cusp/anomalous-dimension structures force \(C_\partial=0\) or provide a concrete nonzero falsifier.
